Resolves #21374

A dialog's minimize, maximize, restore and close now draw as one set: a line, a square, two offset squares and a cross (`fas fa-minus`, `far fa-square`, `far fa-clone`, `fas fa-xmark`). They replace three framed Font Awesome window drawings, and they draw at 1em instead of 1.8em. Each glyph sits in a 28×24 box, so every control stays a 24px target in the neo themes, which unset the header button's own size. Every dialog inherits the change, and `Neo.desktop.AppWindow` needs no line of its own.

Evidence: L3 (live Chromium frames of `dev` at 28fed2adc6 and of this head at the same viewport; computed sizes read in the browser) → L3 required (AC-1, AC-2, AC-4: frames and measurements; AC-5: cold look). Residual: none.

Change class: capability (`feat`). agent-preflight: not hosted here; the pre-commit and pre-push guards ran.

## Cold look

Three readers without context ran one at a time. Two each saw one window frame ([before](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/97973745b00f21f920c0d967160dec249b4ea105/review-evidence/21374/window-dark-before.png?raw=true), [after](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/97973745b00f21f920c0d967160dec249b4ea105/review-evidence/21374/window-dark-after.png?raw=true)) and answered #21348's three questions: what is this screen, how much does it look like a finished product a visitor would trust (1 to 10), and what is its weakest point. The third saw the two neo-dark title bars side by side, unlabelled, as A (after) and B (before).

| Frame | Verdict | Weakest point |
|---|---|---|
| Window, before | 2 of 10; "the window chrome is polished" | the empty body: "no calculator in it" |
| Window, after | 2 of 10; "the title bar and glass-style window look polished" | the empty body |
| Title bars, A and B | A: "one consistent set of thin, evenly spaced, same-weight outline icons"; B's "are heavy and mismatched" | A: "somewhat faint … small next to the bold title", no hover affordance. B: "the three glyphs don't match each other" |

The single-frame question cannot separate the two versions: every reader's weakest point was the empty window body, which #21353 owns. The paired read can, and it names the old set's defect in the words #21348's readers used. Its two points against A have different owners. The glyph colour is unchanged (`--desktop-app-window-icon-color`, and header-icon colour is #21371's), so the thinner strokes read lighter. The missing hover state predates this diff, which adds and removes no hover rule. On this head the close control's background and glyph colour stay identical under the pointer in `examples/desktop/basic` and `examples/dialog`. That is out of scope and noted in a defect-note.

| AC-4 | outside-CI: the frames above, with the desktop window normal and maximized in neo-dark and neo-light, and `examples/dialog` in its own two themes |
| AC-5 | outside-CI: the cold look above |

## Deltas from ticket
- Each glyph sits in a fixed 28×24 box. The ticket asked only for the smaller size, but at 1em the neo themes' `height/min-width: unset` would have shrunk each control to its glyph, below the 24px target.
- `examples/dialog` runs the classic themes, so its frames show theme-light and theme-dark, not neo-dark and neo-light.
- The `dialog.header.Toolbar` JSDoc example showed `fas fa-xmark` as a custom close. That glyph is now the default, so the example shows `far fa-circle-xmark`.

## Test Evidence
The frames, the computed sizes and the hover reading above, all from throwaway Playwright probes that are not committed. All spec coverage runs in CI.
